subject: Processor addition: proposed quiet period, notification timeline, and e-sign flow
messages:
From: Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@cloudsmith.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@cloudsmith.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Notice: addition of 'TelemetryEdge' as a processor - timing & objection window

Hi Grace,

As part of our quarterly review we are adding a small observability vendor, TelemetryEdge, to our processing roster. Attached is the standard processor notice and a short summary of the services (processor_addition_notice.pdf).

Two quick questions for your team:
- What is Redwood's standard quiet period / notification window for new subprocessors (we've seen 30/45/60-day variants)?
- If our customer chooses to object, what is the remediation path you offer (contract redline, temporary suspension, or alternative routing)?

We also have procurement asking whether execution will be via DocuSign or if you require a separate signed addendum.

Appreciate a quick confirmation so we can close internal docs.

Thanks,
Daniel Ortiz
Head of Procurement
CloudSmith

Attachment: processor_addition_notice.pdf (pdf, 94KB)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@cloudsmith.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of 'TelemetryEdge' as a processor - timing & objection window

Thanks for the heads up, Daniel — and for the clear packet. I reviewed the notice and flagged it for legal and commercial. High-level answers below; I’ll follow up with formal language and a DocuSign link.

- Quiet period: Redwood follows a 45-calendar-day notification window by default for new subprocessors. That gives customers time to review and, where applicable, submit objections per the DPA Exhibit B process.
- Objection path: If a customer raises an objection within the window we triage: (1) we confirm the scope of the objection, (2) evaluate technical mitigations or alternate routing where possible, and (3) if the objection remains material we either (a) exclude the specific customer data from processing by the new vendor or (b) negotiate limited concessions in the DPA addendum. Permanent removal is rare but available for narrowly scoped concerns.
- Execution: We can process acceptance via DocuSign for the standard notice + addendum. For customers needing countersigned DPA redlines we will coordinate an e-sign package (DocuSign link) or ship a PDF for signature per CloudSmith preference.

Looping in Laura for any legal nuance. Aditya — fyi for commercial (no pricing impact expected).

Best,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Manager, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of 'TelemetryEdge' as a processor - timing & objection window

Grace — quick legal notes on possible objection scenarios:
- If CloudSmith's customer objects on export controls or a security posture mismatch, we need to escalate to the product security team for an architecture-level mitigation (can add latency, so flag to product).
- For routine privacy objections (data categories, retention), the standard Exhibit B carve-outs + exclusion routing are sufficient.
- DocuSign: redact any vendor-specific IP (if TelemetryEdge attached a proprietary T&C) and attach our Exhibit B revision (redwood_dpa_exhibit_b_revA.docx) for signature.

If CloudSmith wants a shortened window (30 days) we can consider it if TelemetryEdge is low-risk; otherwise we should hold firm at 45 days. Grace — please confirm the risk assessment (low/medium/high) and I can approve a 30-day concession if needed.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Ortiz <daniel.ortiz@cloudsmith.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, procurement@cloudsmith.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 17:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of 'TelemetryEdge' as a processor - timing & objection window

Daniel — thanks again. We completed a preliminary risk review: TelemetryEdge is categorized as low-risk (logs + metrics only, no PII), so commercial flexibility is possible. Attached is the proposed Exhibit B revision and a short internal risk memo.

Proposal:
- Redwood standard: 45-calendar-day notification window.
- For CloudSmith we are willing to shorten to 30-calendar-days given TelemetryEdge's low-risk profile, provided CloudSmith confirms acceptance in writing.
- Execution path: we will send a DocuSign envelope that includes:
  1) acknowledgement of receipt of the processor notice,
  2) the revised Exhibit B (redwood_dpa_exhibit_b_revA.docx), and
  3) an e-sign attestation confirming CloudSmith's right to object within the 30-day window.

DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.com/recipient/ABC12345 (valid for 14 days).
Drive copy of materials: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/privacy/subprocessor-log

If CloudSmith prefers to keep 45 days, we will not require an additional signature and will proceed on the 45-day cadence. Please tell us which option you prefer and whether procurement wants the DocuSign envelope routed to a single signer or multiple signers.

Best,
Grace
Senior Manager, Privacy & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_exhibit_b_revA.docx (docx, 28KB); processor_addition_notice.pdf (pdf, 94KB)
